_doc.what: Per-CardID art-direction prompts for concept_generate.py (Stage 0 of the Siegebound art pipeline, TASK-184 tool / TASK-185 run). Law: CONVENTIONS.md 'Textured mesh law' -> 'Stage 0 - concept generation'.
_doc.schema: The 'prompts' object maps CardID (PascalCase, character-for-character = cards.csv row name = Inbox/<CardID>.png filename) -> an entry: { 'prompt': <required non-empty string, the subject description ONLY>, 'negative_prompt': <optional string>, 'seed': <optional integer for reproducibility> }.
_doc.framing: DO NOT write framing/background/camera words in 'prompt' - concept_generate.py APPENDS a shared PROMPT_SUFFIX (single centered subject, full body, orthographic front three-quarter, plain flat neutral grey background, even lighting, no ground shadow, clean silhouette) to every prompt. Authors describe only the subject so TRELLIS image-to-3D gets a clean single-subject reference.
_doc.negative_prompt: OPTIONAL and only forwarded when the active model supports classifier-free guidance (MODEL_SUPPORTS_NEGATIVE_PROMPT at the top of concept_generate.py). The default model FLUX.1-schnell is guidance-distilled and IGNORES negatives, so negative_prompt is recorded but not sent to it; entries are authored anyway so a later model swap (e.g. SDXL) picks them up. The tool already bakes a shared NEGATIVE_SUFFIX (multiple subjects, crowd, background scenery, props, text, watermark, extra limbs, blurry, low quality); per-entry negatives here are SUBJECT-SPECIFIC only.
_doc.seed: OPTIONAL. Fixes the generation for reproducibility; the CLI --seed overrides it. Every M7 entry carries a distinct seed so a concept is exactly reproducible and a bad roll can be re-rolled deterministically (concept_generate.py <CardID> --force --seed N).
_doc.model_note: The image model/endpoint is a swappable constant (MODEL_ID / PROVIDER) at the top of concept_generate.py - this file is model-agnostic.
_doc.art_direction: GDD §6 'premium stylized' bar: polished stylized low-poly, Warcraft Rumble / Fortnite quality tier. Units ~2.5-3 heads tall with oversized hands/weapons; silhouette readable at 15 m; beveled chunky forms; hand-painted-style textures with gradient shading (darker feet -> lighter shoulders) + rim light; NO flat single-color materials. TEAM-AGNOSTIC palette (cards are player-neutral): base colors stay muted stone / leather / wood / steel, and each unit/building carries ONE small neutral cream cloth accent (tabard/sash/pennant/banner) left uncolored so the runtime team-color slot can recolor it - NO dominant baked red or blue. GoldNode is the exception: an emissive warm-gold economy prop with NO team accent.
